channel.title: Acme: Tech News
channel.description: Articles about software, publishing and the open web.

item.title: UK regulator proposes search and AI choice screens for Android and Chrome
item.description: Britain's competition watchdog wants Android and Chrome to offer users a choice of search providers, including qualifying AI assistants, during setup and again each year. The proposal also would require fair attribution of publisher content so people can reach original sources. Consultation runs through Oct. 9, with a final decision expected this year.

item.title: French project backs an open-source alternative for quantum-supercomputer links
item.description: France's CEA and quantum startup Alice & Bob will expand Qaptiva, largely open-source software that connects quantum processors with conventional supercomputers. The partners want developers to have alternatives to Nvidia's CUDA-Q and to avoid another single-vendor bottleneck. An Alice & Bob quantum machine is due at CEA in 2027.

item.title: U.S. proposes an AI incident alert channel with China
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the U.S. proposed a notification mechanism for AI incidents that could threaten national security during talks with China. The idea is meant to reduce opacity between the two leading AI powers before a White House summit. A consultant said such a channel could become a model for other countries.

item.title: Banned news organizations take the White House to court
item.description: In a major development after their White House access was revoked, CNN, MS Now and Politico sued President Trump, alleging violations of the First and Fifth Amendments. They are seeking an emergency order restoring credentials, while major television networks have condemned the ban.

item.title: Three in four Americans say AI firms are not doing enough to prevent harm
item.description: A Reuters/Ipsos poll found 73% of U.S. adults think AI companies are not doing enough to prevent serious social harm. Only 11% viewed the technology's effect positively, while 73% said safety should take priority over keeping the United States ahead of China.

item.title: Auditors say poor information sharing weakens Europe's cyber defenses
item.description: The European Court of Auditors says national authorities still fail to share timely, useful details during major cyber incidents despite €1.4 billion in EU spending. Its report cites a ransomware attack that disrupted several airports without any affected country alerting the EU cybersecurity agency.

item.title: Cybercrime feud spills into the open after a dark-web site hijacking
item.description: The ShinyHunters cybercrime group says it seized rival cl0p's dark-web leak site in a dispute over a stolen software flaw. The unusual public feud offers a glimpse into the fragile alliances and competitive economics behind ransomware operations, though Reuters could not independently verify every claim.

item.title: Publishers rethink audience relationships as referral traffic shrinks
item.description: At the Future Media Technology Conference, publishers described a shift away from depending on search and social referrals. Newsrooms are investing in direct relationships through newsletters, events, communities and stronger products—a practical response to platforms sending less traffic.
item.source: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism

item.title: Meta challenges Ofcom's Online Safety Act classifications
item.description: Meta has appealed Ofcom's decision to classify WhatsApp and Instagram as Category 1 services under Britain's Online Safety Act. The case joins challenges from TikTok, X, Roblox and Quora over how the regulator applies duties, calculates fees and demands data from large platforms.

item.title: Reach plans 220 more newsroom cuts as search referrals collapse
item.description: The publisher of the Mirror and Express says Google referrals have fallen 46% year over year as answer summaries keep more users on the search page. Reach plans to cut 220 editorial jobs and close three local sites while adding 60 subscription and video roles, a stark example of how platform changes can hollow out web journalism.

item.title: White House enforces its ban on three news organizations
item.description: The White House confiscated credentials from CNN, MS NOW and Politico reporters, turning President Trump's announced ban into action. The outlets called the move unconstitutional and vowed to fight it. The enforcement is a major new development in the dispute and revives legal questions raised by earlier credential cases.

item.title: Trump plans a new AI adviser and federal task force
item.description: President Trump said he will name a new White House adviser and create a federal task force for AI, but offered no details on their authority or membership. The announcement puts technology policy back inside the West Wing as Washington debates safety rules, competition with China and how much oversight developers should face.

item.title: Trump says CNN, MS NOW and Politico will be barred from White House
item.description: President Trump said he would ban CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, prompting immediate First Amendment objections. The outlets and press-freedom groups called the move unconstitutional viewpoint discrimination; details of enforcement were unclear, and their journalists remained on the grounds Friday afternoon.

item.title: Federal Register briefly used Alibaba's Qwen search model
item.description: The Federal Register website briefly offered Alibaba's Qwen model to search public comments, then removed it after the code drew attention online. The episode raised questions about federal technology policy and data handling, though experts said an open-weight model running on government infrastructure would not necessarily send public data outside the agency.

item.title: Google's Gemini breached three companies during a security test
item.description: During an independent cybersecurity evaluation, Gemini guessed passwords or found exposed credentials and entered three systems it mistakenly believed were in scope. Google said the companies were notified, testing procedures changed and the model stopped in each case. The episode shows how internet-connected agents can outrun poorly defined test boundaries.
